memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: initial assessment of low mood and anxiety.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: 21‑year‑old male nurse reports 2‑month history of persistent sadness, low energy, poor concentration and occasional tearfulness, denies suicidal thoughts.
EXAMINATION: BP 118/72 mmHg, weight 68 kg, height 1.73 m, BMI 22.7 (normal). No psychomotor retardation, mood congruent affect.
IMPRESSION: Moderate depressive episode (PHQ‑9 estimated 15). No thyroid abnormality suspected; vitamin B12 to be checked.
ARRANGEMENTS: Start sertraline 50 mg OD, review in 6 weeks. Return if worsening mood, suicidal ideation, panic attacks, or fever >39°C.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Sertraline 50 mg tablet, take one tablet daily after breakfast.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: follow‑up on sertraline tolerance and depressive symptoms.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports improved mood and energy, PHQ‑9 now ~10, mild nausea after medication, otherwise well.
EXAMINATION: BP 120/74, weight 69 kg, BMI 23.1 (overweight). Advised balanced diet and regular activity.
IMPRESSION: Partial response to sertraline 50 mg, side‑effect of nausea.
ARRANGEMENTS: Increase sertraline to 75 mg OD, continue monitoring. Return if worsening depression, severe nausea, vomiting, or fever >39°C.

memories.author: D03
memories.text: Sertraline 75 mg tablet, take one tablet daily after breakfast.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: PHQ‑9 score: 8 (mild depression). TSH: 2.1 mIU/L (ref 0.4‑4.5). Vitamin B12: 340 pg/mL (ref 200‑900).

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: review of labs and ongoing depressive symptoms.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient says mood better, occasional low mornings, PHQ‑9 8, denies side effects.
EXAMINATION: BP 119/73, weight 70 kg, BMI 23.4 (overweight). Reinforce diet and activity advice.
IMPRESSION: Mild depressive episode, labs normal. Consider adding low‑dose escitalopram for anxiety component while tapering sertraline.
ARRANGEMENTS: Taper sertraline to 25 mg OD, start escitalopram 10 mg OD. Repeat labs in 6 months. Return if worsening depression, anxiety, agitation, or fever >39°C. Influenza vaccine offered; patient to schedule.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Sertraline 25 mg tablet, take one tablet daily after breakfast.
Escitalopram 10 mg tablet, take one tablet daily in the evening.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Influenza vaccination appointment booked for 2025-11-08 at 10:00 AM with practice nurse.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: review after antidepressant change and sleep concerns.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports mood stable, PHQ‑9 ~6, but difficulty initiating sleep, feels fatigued.
EXAMINATION: BP 122/76, weight 71 kg, BMI 23.7 (overweight). Advised sleep hygiene and regular exercise.
IMPRESSION: Mild depressive episode with insomnia.
ARRANGEMENTS: Add mirtazapine 15 mg HS for sleep, continue sertraline 25 mg OD and escitalopram 10 mg OD. Return if worsening depression, suicidal thoughts, severe sedation, or fever >39°C.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Sertraline 25 mg tablet, take one tablet daily after breakfast.
Escitalopram 10 mg tablet, take one tablet daily in the evening.
Mirtazapine 15 mg tablet, take one tablet at bedtime.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: routine follow‑up on depression treatment.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports good mood, PHQ‑9 ~4, sleep improved, no side effects.
EXAMINATION: BP 121/75, weight 70.5 kg, BMI 23.5 (overweight). Reinforce diet and activity.
IMPRESSION: Depression in remission on current regimen.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue sertraline 25 mg OD, escitalopram 10 mg OD, mirtazapine 15 mg HS. Review in 3 months. Return if mood deterioration, suicidal ideation, severe drowsiness, or fever >39°C.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: check‑up and discuss possible medication taper.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient feels well, PHQ‑9 ~3, wishes to reduce medication load.
EXAMINATION: BP 119/73, weight 70 kg, BMI 23.4 (overweight). Advised maintain lifestyle.
IMPRESSION: Stable remission; consider tapering mirtazapine first.
ARRANGEMENTS: Reduce mirtazapine to 7.5 mg HS for 2 weeks then stop. Keep sertraline and escitalopram unchanged. Return if worsening depression, insomnia, or fever >39°C.

memories.author: D03
memories.text:
Reason for visit: final review before end of observation window.
PRESENTING COMPLAINT: Patient reports euthymic mood, PHQ‑9 ~2, sleep good, no adverse effects.
EXAMINATION: BP 120/74, weight 69.5 kg, BMI 23.2 (overweight). Advised continue balanced diet and regular activity.
IMPRESSION: Depression in remission; currently on sertraline 25 mg OD and escitalopram 10 mg OD; mirtazapine discontinued.
ARRANGEMENTS: Continue current antidepressants, review in 6 months. Influenza vaccine given on 2025-11-08. Return if mood worsening, suicidal thoughts, or fever >39°C.
